headline: Crade lets ChatGPT and Claude see your screen on Mac and Windows, eliminating screenshots
summary: Crade is a new Mac and Windows app that floats over your screen, capturing it on demand and piping it directly to your OpenAI or Anthropic account, streamlining AI interactions.
details: Interacting with AI models like ChatGPT and Claude often involves a tedious workflow of taking screenshots, switching apps, pasting, and asking. This repetitive process can consume significant time for users who do it dozens of times a day.

Crade aims to solve this by providing a floating Mac and Windows application. It captures your screen on demand and sends the content directly to your own ChatGPT or Claude account, removing the need for manual screenshots and tab switching.

In 'Bring Your Own' (BYO) mode, Crade ensures user privacy by directly piping screenshots from your machine to OpenAI or Anthropic via their respective CLIs. This means Crade itself does not sit in the middle of the data transfer.

The app achieves its 'always-on-top' functionality on macOS by asserting a high window level (kCGAssistiveTechHighWindowLevel), re-asserting it every 500ms to maintain priority. For Windows, Qt.WindowStaysOnTopHint is sufficient.

Crade was developed using Python and PyQt6, a deliberate choice over Electron. While this presented challenges like finicky PyInstaller distribution and a dated default UI, the developers opted for it despite a smaller talent pool for desktop Python.

Crade offers a free tier for daily use, with Pro ($7.99/month) and Premium ($19.99/month) subscriptions available. These paid tiers provide higher usage caps and an 'Agent mode' that grants the AI access to the file system and shell.
caption:

headline: Apple and Intel are working together to build chips in America, says President Trump
summary: President Trump confirmed a previously rumored partnership between Apple and Intel. This collaboration aims to manufacture chips domestically in the United States.
details: President Trump took to TruthSocial to confirm a significant partnership between Apple and Intel. This collaboration focuses on building semiconductor chips within America, a move that had been previously rumored.

While specific details regarding the scale and timeline of this manufacturing initiative were not provided, the announcement highlights a potential strategic shift. It underscores a growing emphasis on domestic production for critical technology components by major tech companies.
